extraction.name: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.description: MMMU is a benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. It includes 11.5K meticulously collected multimodal questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks, covering six core disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering. These questions span 30 subjects and 183 subfields, comprising 30 highly heterogeneous image types, such as charts, diagrams, maps, tables, music sheets, and chemical structures. Unlike existing benchmarks, MMMU focuses on advanced perception and reasoning with domain-specific knowledge, challenging models to perform tasks akin to those faced by experts.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue, Yuansheng Ni, Kai Zhang, Tianyu Zheng, Ruoqi Liu, Ge Zhang, Samuel Stevens, Dongfu Jiang, Weiming Ren, Yuxuan Sun, Cong Wei, Botao Yu, Ruibin Yuan, Renliang Sun, Ming Yin, Boyuan Zheng, Zhenzhu Yang, Yibo Liu, Wenhao Huang, Huan Sun, Yu Su, Wenhu Chen
extraction.citeAs: MMMU: A Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Expert AGI
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The MMMU dataset was meticulously curated through a three-stage process: 1) Subject Selection: 30 subjects were selected from six disciplines based on the principle that visual inputs should be commonly adopted in the subjects to provide valuable information. 2) Data Collection: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given the arising data contamination concerns of foundation models, the annotators were advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks. This process resulted in a diverse collection of 13K questions from various sources. 3) Data Quality Control: To further control the quality of the data, two steps of data cleaning were performed. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involved distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step required authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations were found. The third and final stage involved categorizing the problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, were excluded from the benchmark.

extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The data collection process for the MMMU dataset was conducted over several months, with the final dataset compiled in 2023. The dataset includes questions from college exams, quizzes, and textbooks spanning six common disciplines: Art & Design, Business, Science, Health & Medicine, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data preprocessing protocol for the MMMU dataset involved several steps to ensure quality and consistency. 1) Duplicate Removal: Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. 2) Format and Typo Checking: The problems were distributed among different co-authors for format and typo checking. This step required authors to ensure adherence to a standardized format, undertaking necessary corrections where deviations were found. 3) Difficulty Categorization: The problems were categorized into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with the design criteria due to their simplistic nature, were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The data annotation protocol for the MMMU dataset involved a structured process to ensure accuracy and consistency. 1) Question Collection: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors collected multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources. They created new questions based on their expertise where necessary. 2) Quality Control: The collected questions were reviewed for quality and adherence to guidelines. Lexical overlap and source URL similarity were used to identify potential duplicates, which were then reviewed and eliminated. 3) Format and Typo Checking: The problems were distributed among different co-authors for format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format. 4) Difficulty Categorization: The problems were categorized into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy, were excluded from the benchmark.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The data annotation platform for the MMMU dataset involved a user-friendly web interface developed by Tianyu Zheng. This interface facilitated the data annotation and verification process, significantly improving the workflow for data curation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The data annotation analysis for the MMMU dataset involved a detailed review process to ensure quality and consistency. Ambiguities or unclear data instances were flagged for a detailed review process. These questions were collaboratively examined in team meetings to establish a standardized approach for annotation. The analysis also included error categorization and case studies to identify common errors and areas for improvement.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: The MMMU dataset includes annotations for each item, with the number of human labels per dataset item varying based on the complexity and type of the question. For multiple-choice questions, the correct answer is annotated, and for open-ended questions, the correct answer and explanation are provided.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: The annotators for the MMMU dataset were over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors. The annotators were instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. The annotators were also advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: The MMMU dataset utilized machine annotation tools for data preprocessing and quality control. These tools included lexical overlap and source URL similarity checks to identify potential duplicates, as well as format and typo checking to ensure adherence to a standardized format.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The MMMU dataset is maintained and updated through a structured process. The dataset is released under the MIT License, and the authors have provided a version change log to document updates and improvements. The dataset is designed to be a live dataset, with ongoing efforts to ensure quality and consistency.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The MMMU dataset is designed to evaluate multimodal models on tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. The dataset aims to push the boundaries of what large multimodal models (LMMs) can achieve and stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence. The dataset also aims to monitor the progress towards Expert AGI and provide a comprehensive benchmark that aligns with the expectations of skilled adults in these fields.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The MMMU dataset, while comprehensive, may carry biases due to its manual curation process and the focus on college-level subjects. The dataset may not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI as per the definition, and there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the '90th percentile of skilled adults.' The dataset also focuses on college-level knowledge, which may not fully represent the breadth and depth of expert-level tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The MMMU dataset has several limitations. 1) Manual Curation Bias: The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI. 2) Data Contamination: The dataset may include questions with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks, which could lead to data contamination concerns. 3) Limited Representation: The dataset focuses on college-level knowledge and may not fully represent the breadth and depth of expert-level tasks. 4) Non-recommended Uses: The dataset is not recommended for testing Expert AGI as per the definition, and there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and the '90th percentile of skilled adults.'
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The MMMU dataset is designed for evaluating multimodal models on tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning. The dataset can be used for training, testing, and validation of large multimodal models (LMMs). The dataset aims to push the boundaries of what LMMs can achieve and stimulate the community to build next-generation multimodal foundation models towards expert artificial general intelligence. The dataset also aims to monitor the progress towards Expert AGI and provide a comprehensive benchmark that aligns with the expectations of skilled adults in these fields.
